summary: Independent review of the updated Release Intelligence v2.0.0-GA GOLDEN BUILD ZIP SHA256 d9d070f37cc420eb96a0708bfb5f7e374ecc337cfc55806760b87df0c8b8572f. All 29 packaged files byte-match source. The reusable runtime policy and instruction document match exactly, prioritizing current-month engineer and sprint evidence, goals as intent, and supported risk/recovery context. SDK and native monthly paths reject task inventories in both current and prior paragraphs, allow one correction within their shared deadlines, and return no ready draft after failure. The editor applies only nonempty ready results, preserving original text and unsaved state otherwise. Current health can support only an exact generic blocked-state statement and is excluded from historical grounding. The identified inventory bypasses are fixed. Independently executed all 46 focused monthly, AI, and grounding tests successfully. No blocking issues remain. Overall application risk remains High under the existing rubric assessment.
caveats: Narrative and factual checks remain strict linguistic heuristics, not a proof of complete grounding or coverage. They can reject valid paraphrases or miss other misleading formulations; human review of outcomes, timing, scope, and recovery plans remains necessary.
Current epic health is a fresh snapshot, not proof of an earlier or future state. It cannot establish a cause, completion date, deployment, release, or recovery plan by itself.

When evidence or model output cannot satisfy the contract, monthly generation intentionally produces no editor draft. Existing text is retained; users must review source evidence, edit manually, or retry.
Automatic correction can add one model request. SDK attempts share a 60-second deadline and native attempts share 12 seconds; cancellation cannot guarantee upstream model work stops.

Existing Slack prepare/copy-only behavior and unverified native paste/identity, chronological rich-text fail-closed behavior, usage completeness, preview caching, refresh concurrency, journal growth, revision conflicts, non-atomic updates, preference semantics, host/catalog/history limits, and AllUsers sharing caveats remain.
Current GUS Apps host metadata still relies on verified-definition snapshots; future automatic list-column detection remains unavailable without live list-view REST capability.

This review combined static source/artifact inspection with 46 independently executed focused tests. The implementing agent reported all 175 Node tests passed and the final browser rerun passed, including colon-inventory correction, repeated-invalid preservation of editor/unsaved/source state, and explicit-save persistence after reload. Those full suites, actual native or SDK production-model behavior, hosted browser behavior, remote publication, and golden-tag movement were not independently verified.
